name: Family Residency for Spouses and Children of Paraguayan Citizens

requirement_groups.name: Spouse or child of a Paraguayan citizen (Ley 2193/2003)

requirements.blocker_text: Under Ley 2193/2003, a foreign spouse or foreign child (of any age, including adults) of a Paraguayan citizen qualifies for a distinct family-based residency pathway, processed via SEDERREC (the repatriation-support agency) rather than the standard economic-solvency track: obtain a SEDERREC repatriation certificate, receive a national ID card from the National Police, then apply for Permanent Residency at Migraciones within a strict 90-day deadline from receiving the cedula. Required: valid passport, apostilled birth/marriage certificates, apostilled criminal background check, and the Paraguayan family member's own cedula. No provision was found covering PARENTS or GRANDPARENTS of a Paraguayan citizen as qualifying relatives -- a real, disclosed absence, not this dataset's assumption.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a SEDERREC repatriation certificate, get a national ID card, and file for Permanent Residency at Migraciones within 90 days of receiving the cedula.

sources.title: Plan B Expat -- Ley 2193/2003 spouse/child pathway and Ley 6984/22 Article 48 repatriated-national family pathway, with the 90-day filing deadline

GENUINE, DISCLOSED ABSENCE: no route was found for PARENTS or GRANDPARENTS of a Paraguayan citizen to join them in Paraguay -- only spouses and children (any age) under Ley 2193/2003, and separately spouses/children/grandchildren-under-18 of REPATRIATED Paraguayan nationals specifically under Ley 6984/22 Article 48 (a narrower category this dataset did not model as its own file, since it is a subset of the same general family-residency mechanism rather than a structurally distinct route). This grants Permanent Residency directly (pr_after_months: 0), distinct from every other Paraguay route in this build, which requires a temporary-to-permanent conversion first. family_can_join set to false at the outcome level: this route IS the family-joining mechanism itself, so it has no further dependent-of-the-applicant provision to report.
